figures.finding: Belize publishes no production rebate or film fund; the Belize Film Commission licenses each shoot (letter of intent, then a Film License application with its fee, approved in 2 to 3 working days), requires a Belizean or resident local coordinator for the whole production, arranges duty exemptions on equipment listed two weeks ahead, and lets crew work without permits for stays under 30 days (longer stays pay for a permit or get an exemption through the Commission).

value.localCoordinator: mandatory, Belizean citizen or legal resident
value.equipmentDutyExemption: list at least two weeks before arrival

sources.said: The completed application with the required fee and documentation can be submitted to the Belize Film Commission by the Local Coordinator before arrival or upon arrival of a film crew in Belize. The approval process is usually 2-3 days working days after receipt of the application. … The services of a local coordinator are mandatory for any filming done in Belize. … A local coordinator is defined as a Belizean citizen or legal resident of Belize. … must be sent at least two weeks before arrival to ensure duty exemptions. … Work permits are not required for the crew if they will stay less than 30 days in the country. However, if the production will last 30 days and over, the company will have to either: a) Pay for a work permit or b) The Belize Film Commission will apply for WORK PERMIT EXEMPTIONS.

figures.finding: Belize's local film industry is small: the Film Commissioner's own company Veritas Productions is described as producing original Belizean films, and the Commission's stated aim is for Belizeans to make their own films.

sources.said: Veritas Productions, which produces original Belizean films … so that Belizeans can make their own films and create a distinct identity for Belize and Belizeans on film.
